messages:
ashley: quick FYI — canary-04 showed p95 up ~18% after we reduced micro-batch interval to 1.2ms. suspect kernel thrash + KV miss rate spike. attaching short profiler excerpt.

raul: do we have kernel-switch counts and kv-hit ratio from the same window?

ashley: pasted profiler snippet:
```
p50: 7.2ms -> 6.8ms
p95: 21.4ms -> 25.3ms
kernels_switched: 342 -> 1101
kv_cache_hit: 0.87 -> 0.61
```

kevin: whoa kernel switches x3. that smells like fragmentation in kernel selection when token budget decreased. did we change token_budget target for the canary?

ashley: yes — token_budget target was 256 -> 128 to try reduce per-request compute. thought it would help but looks like it's increasing kernel fragmentation and causing mid-request kernel handoffs.

ashok: suggestion: 1) bump coalesce_delay from 1.2ms -> 1.8ms, 2) add small jitter scaling (0.2 * base) to spread arrivals, 3) set `kernel_hold_time_ms=5` to avoid switching kernels mid-request. also add a gating rule: if kv_cache_hit < 0.7 then prefer larger token_budget for that queue.

perf-bot: perf run uploaded: https://perf.redwood/internal/trace/1711112222 — kernel_hold_time experiment reduced kernel switches by ~65% and kv_hit recovered to 0.79, p95 improved but not fully recovered. :thumbsup:

raul: can we also log a compact "kernel_reason" with values like `KV_MISS` / `SEQ_LONG` / `BATCH_FULL` for each selection decision? even a single byte code per decision would help correlate.

kevin: +1. and schedule a short sweep: token_budget targets [128,160,192,224] x coalesce_delay [1.2,1.8,2.5] with jitter {0,0.2*base}. keep micro-batch interval at 1.2ms for baseline vs 1.8ms variant.

ashley: I'll run the sweep tomorrow morning and seed with a small traffic shadow. tagging @eng-sre to monitor canary if it spikes. :rocket:

perf-bot: note: canary baseline pinned to model v2.3.4, runtime commit a1b2c3. artifacts will be attached after sweep.

ashley: thanks — will post a short matrix of results. if we see persistent KV thrash we should revert token_budget to previous and follow up with kernel selection rule audit.
